prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Alder Creek Electrical Distribution Substation supplies transformer/feeder bays/distribution circuits within approved limits.
Bay Automation Controller (Juniper), including North Bay Controller/South Bay Controller, produces Bay Status Digest; timestamps local changes; applies permissives/interlocks. Breaker Control Unit executes authorized requests subject to modes/authority/selection/interlocks/availability/procedures; local authority prevails.
Feeder Protection Relay (Tandem) independently protects/trips using approved settings; produces Relay Diagnostic Note. Station Supervisory Control System (Glasswing) produces Alarm Acknowledgement Slip; separates current indications from archival evidence; local indications prevail. Station Gateway carries authorized remote communications; verify currency after outages.
Satellite Time Receiver (Bluefin) distributes time; produces Clock Drift Snapshot; reference-loss invokes device-specific holdover and synchronized/degraded/unavailable quality, not evidence deletion. Timing validates neither measurements nor protection.
Station DC System powers protection/automation; produces Battery Load Test Record for engineering-record retention.
Sequence Event Archive (Orchard), authoritative repository, preserves source/event-time/receipt-time/quality/original-order; distinguishes uncertain continuity/time and corrected/estimated times. Retains configuration/access-history; role-restricts access; audits administration; applies retention schedules/investigation holds until authorized release. Check capacity/ingestion/recoverability; test readability/timestamp/quality restoration; protect additional backup.
Engineering Workstation restricts revision-controlled configurations/history to engineering; produces Settings Review Receipt; provides approved search/filter/export tools. Bound queries by station/equipment/time; exports preserve timestamps/quality; label derived ordering; separate conclusions.
Protection Relay Engineer (Larkspur) compares events/relay indications and uses Relay Diagnostic Note for analysis; study-based coordinated revisions require independent approval, approved work-window, installed-settings comparison/testing; unresolved discrepancies block release.
Substation Supervisor oversees authorization/procedures/availability. Switching Desk Coordinator (Keystone) maintains station-wide switching plan across both bays; checks requests against clearances/work; confirms handback; evidence remains reviewable. Control Room Operator submits equipment/change/timing requests, reviews event sequences, coordinates access/suspension/resumption.
Maintenance Remote Terminal supports approved maintenance without overriding local authority.
Substation Field Crew (Cinder) verifies authorization/hazards/boundaries/equipment/isolation/absence-of-energy—not screens alone; logs presence; maintains communications; stops/escalates uncertainty/loss; sends Breaker Inspection Tag recording condition/time; accounts personnel/tools/connections before completion.

New part:
S127: The Substation Supervisor resolves priority conflicts and confirms the operational authority for exceptional switching conditions.
S128: Approved switching sequences identify the required order of actions, hold points, and conditions for stopping work.
S129: The North Bay Controller manages control and interlocking functions assigned to the north bay under the approved sequence.
S130: The North Bay Controller blocks a close command when its local interlocks indicate that the bay is not ready.
S131: The South Bay Controller manages the corresponding control and interlocking functions assigned to the south bay.
S132: The two controllers have separate equipment scopes and do not substitute for one another when executing a switching sequence.
S133: The bay boundary defines which controller may operate each device and which indications are used to confirm its state.
S134: Equipment shared across the boundary requires explicit coordination before a switching action can affect either bay.
S135: The Bay Automation Controller presents bay control status while preserving the separate operating scopes of the two controllers.
S136: The Breaker Control Unit executes permitted breaker commands only when the applicable control conditions are satisfied.
S137: The North Protection Panel supports protection functions for the north-side equipment within its assigned scope.
S138: The Transformer Protection Panel retains its protection authority independently of the bay switching sequence.
S139: The Station Supervisory Control System uses the status digest to review current station operating conditions.
S140: The Sequence Event Archive receives the Clock Drift Snapshot for event-time correlation.
S141: The Switching Desk Coordinator produces the Isolation Boundary Card for the planned work.
S142: The Station Gateway produces the Protocol Retry Summary for communication review.
S143: Larkspur reviews protection coordination questions that could affect the planned switching sequence.
S144: Bluefin provides the station time reference used to align recorded event times.
S145: The Substation Field Crew confirms device identity and local conditions before carrying out an authorized operation.
S146: After the Switching Desk Coordinator confirms operational handback, state-change evidence remains available for authorized engineering review.
S147: Alarm indications are assessed according to protection significance, equipment condition, and the potential effect on service.
S148: The Control Room Operator reviews the alarm priority, source, time, and associated bay indications before deciding on a response.
S149: The operator distinguishes a new alarm from a standing condition and checks whether related indications support the same assessment.
S150: For a protection operation or an unexplained equipment state, the Control Room Operator treats the condition as requiring prompt investigation.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
